questions.explanation: Building takes long lead times and capital and requires proving controls to auditors. Colocation and cloud support encryption and access control, and building is rarely cheaper at small scale.

questions.question: A cloud web application has a server-side request forgery flaw. An attacker uses it to query the workload's local metadata address and obtains temporary credentials for the instance role. Which mitigation reduces the impact MOST effectively?
options: Move the application to a different availability zone so the attacker's request is routed elsewhere
Rotate the application's TLS certificate every day, which changes the identity but not the credentials stolen
Increase the instance size so the workload can absorb the larger number of malicious requests
Use the session-token version of the metadata service and give the role only the permissions it needs
questions.explanation: Token-protected metadata access and least-privilege roles block both the request pattern and the blast radius. Instance size, zone placement and certificate rotation do not address credential theft through SSRF.

questions.question: After an incident the team needs to prove which payload an attacker sent to a database server, but flow logs show only addresses and ports. What would have provided this evidence?
options: A longer retention period for billing records and the cost allocation reports of the account
A larger number of availability zones for the application tier of the workload
Targeted packet capture through traffic mirroring on the affected segment
More frequent patching of the provider's management console and its client tools
questions.explanation: Packet capture records content-level data that flow logs omit, and traffic mirroring supplies it in virtual networks. Billing retention, console patching and more zones do not capture payloads.

questions.question: An architect must choose between sharing risk and transferring risk for a major outage of a critical vendor. Which action BEST represents risk sharing?
options: Accepting the risk without a recorded decision, owner or review date for the residual exposure
Removing the workload from the business entirely, which is risk avoidance rather than sharing
Declining to assess the vendor at all, on the grounds that its certificate covers the risk
Contracting a second provider to carry part of the workload with a split of consequences
questions.explanation: Sharing divides the impact with another party by contract or arrangement. Not assessing, removing the workload (avoidance) and silent acceptance are different or unsound treatments.

questions.question: A BIA states that during recovery the order system needs only about half its normal capacity to keep the business viable. What does this requirement describe?
options: Maximum tolerable downtime
Annualized rate of occurrence
Recovery point objective
Recovery service level
questions.explanation: The recovery service level is the share of normal capacity required while recovering and allows a smaller recovery environment. RPO is about data loss, MTD is about time and ARO is a risk frequency.

questions.question: A team wants to validate its disaster recovery procedures with minimal risk to production, but a document review alone has not exposed any issues. Which next test is MOST appropriate?
options: Deleting the primary site in production to prove that the backup works under real conditions
No further testing, since a thorough document review proves that the procedures will work
A full interruption of production during business hours, to see whether the recovery procedures hold up
A tabletop exercise where participants walk through a realistic scenario
questions.explanation: A tabletop is a low-risk step up in realism from a document review. A full interruption carries high risk and no testing leaves assumptions unproven.

questions.question: A risk analyst values an application server at 200000, estimates that an outage would destroy 25 percent of that value and expects it twice a year. What is the annualized loss expectancy?
questions.explanation: Single loss expectancy is 200000 times 0.25, giving 50000; multiplied by an annual rate of 2 the annualized loss expectancy is 100000. The other values come from missing one of the steps.

questions.question: A cloud security team must show an auditor how an attacker moved from a stolen developer token to an object store. Which capability is MOST essential?
options: Encryption of the finished audit report with a key held by the audit committee
Faster processors on the logging servers so that events are written to disk more quickly
Larger log retention on a single local disk attached to each of the application servers
Correlation of identity, management-plane and storage access logs across sources
questions.explanation: Correlating events across identity, control-plane and data-plane logs reveals the chain of actions. Retention on one local disk, report encryption and processor speed do not link events.

questions.question: Which TWO design choices improve the resilience of a cloud data center's environmental systems? (Choose two.)
options: Clean-agent or pre-action fire suppression suited to equipment rooms
Redundant cooling units with monitored temperature sensors
Water-based sprinklers that discharge on every detector alarm
A single air conditioning unit shared by all halls
Locating the generator fuel supply in a single shared tank without monitoring
questions.explanation: Cooling redundancy with monitoring and equipment-safe fire suppression protect continuity. A single cooling unit, indiscriminate water discharge and an unmonitored single fuel point create failure points.

questions.question: Which TWO controls MOST directly protect the confidentiality of data traveling between workloads in different virtual networks? (Choose two.)
options: A larger instance type for the sending workload
Mutual TLS between services
Disabling flow logs
An IPsec VPN or private link with encryption layered on top
A VLAN tag on the traffic
questions.explanation: Encryption in transit, whether TLS or IPsec, protects confidentiality. VLAN tags only separate traffic and are not encryption, and instance size or logging settings do not encrypt.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about qualitative and quantitative risk analysis are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: The two methods cannot be combined in one program
Qualitative analysis ranks risks on scales and is quicker but more subjective
Quantitative analysis supports cost-benefit decisions when reliable data exists
Qualitative analysis produces annualized loss expectancy in currency
Quantitative analysis never needs asset values
questions.explanation: Quantitative uses values and probabilities for cost-benefit; qualitative uses ratings. Many programs combine them.

questions.question: Two carriers entering a data center through the same trench give full protection against a single cable cut.
questions.explanation: Physical path diversity is required; carriers sharing one trench share a failure point.

questions.question: The Uptime Institute Tier III classification describes a concurrently maintainable site.
questions.explanation: Tier III allows planned maintenance without shutting down IT load; Tier IV adds fault tolerance.

questions.question: Annualized loss expectancy equals single loss expectancy multiplied by the annualized rate of occurrence.
questions.explanation: ALE = SLE x ARO; compare the reduction against the annual cost of the safeguard.

questions.question: A VLAN encrypts traffic between its members.
questions.explanation: VLANs segment broadcast domains but provide no encryption; misconfigured trunks can even enable VLAN hopping.

questions.question: A product team wants security requirements that can be verified in testing and that scale with the sensitivity of each application, from low-risk internal tools to payment services. Which resource is MOST appropriate as the basis?
options: A list of programming languages approved by the architects and the versions of each they allow
A single penetration test report from last year
The OWASP Top 10 used as a pass or fail certificate
The OWASP Application Security Verification Standard with its assurance levels
questions.explanation: ASVS provides testable requirements at graduated levels. The Top 10 is an awareness list rather than a standard to certify against, an old test report is not a requirement set and a language list does not define security.

questions.question: A developer team building a customer-facing assistant that calls internal tools wants a risk list tailored to large language model applications. Which source is MOST relevant?
options: The OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
A generic list of network ports and the services that traditionally use each of them on servers
The CWE Top 25 alone, because it is the only list that ranks weaknesses by severity
The OWASP Top 10 for web applications alone, since it already covers every application type
questions.explanation: The LLM list covers prompt injection, excessive agency, output handling and model poisoning that general web lists omit. The web Top 10 and CWE list are useful but not tailored, and port lists are unrelated.

questions.question: A new feature lets a user reset a password. In design review a security engineer proposes a list of ways an attacker could misuse it: enumerating accounts, flooding the endpoint and replaying a token. What is this technique?
options: Abuse case analysis feeding negative tests
Software composition analysis of dependencies
Functional regression testing of the happy path
Capacity planning for the endpoint
questions.explanation: Abuse cases describe malicious use and become negative tests. Happy-path regression checks intended behavior, capacity planning concerns load and composition analysis inspects libraries.

questions.question: A threat model produced a long list of threats categorized with STRIDE. The team now needs to rank them so the highest risks are fixed first. Which scoring model is named in the outline for this purpose?
options: PASTA
SAFECode
ATASM
DREAD
questions.explanation: DREAD scores damage, reproducibility, exploitability, affected users and discoverability. PASTA and ATASM are modeling methods and SAFECode is a body of practice guidance.

questions.question: An organization wants a threat modeling approach tied to business objectives that simulates attacker behavior in several defined stages. Which method fits BEST?
options: CVSS
PASTA
DREAD
STRIDE
questions.explanation: PASTA is a seven-stage, risk-centric process linking business goals to attack simulation. DREAD and CVSS score threats or vulnerabilities and STRIDE categorizes threat types.

questions.question: A team sees that its code scanner flags a library problem in release 4.2, but the release cannot be reproduced because the configuration and dependency versions were edited by hand on a server. Which practice would have prevented this?
options: Software configuration management with version control and tagged, reproducible builds
Disabling the code scanner for older releases so that only new releases generate findings
Giving every developer root access to production so that fixes can be applied directly on servers
Moving the application to a larger virtual machine
questions.explanation: Version-controlled code, configuration and dependencies make any build reproducible and traceable. Turning off scanning, sizing up and widening access make things worse.

questions.question: A team can see the source code of a SaaS integration and tests its logic for injection flaws without running it. Which testing category is this?
options: White-box testing using static analysis
Load testing for performance
Black-box testing using fuzzing
Gray-box testing without code access
questions.explanation: Inspecting source without running it is static, white-box testing. Fuzzing runs the program from outside, gray-box testing has partial knowledge and load testing is non-functional performance work.

questions.question: A company relies on an open-source library that a single maintainer abandoned, with a license that requires publishing derived source. What is the MOST appropriate response?
options: Allow each team to pull whichever copy of the library it prefers from public sources
Review license obligations and maintainer health, then replace or fork under a managed process
Keep using it unchanged, because open-source software carries no license or maintenance obligations for the user
Remove all versioning information to avoid disclosure
questions.explanation: Open-source intake includes license review and health assessment, with a plan to replace or maintain. Ignoring obligations, hiding version data and unrestricted downloads increase risk.

questions.question: A build pipeline deploys whatever artifact a developer uploads to a shared registry. An attacker uploads a modified image to the registry. Which control would block it at deployment time?
options: Signature verification against trusted keys with provenance checks
A longer retention period for build logs and the records of every pipeline run
Renaming the registry repository and publishing the new name to every developer
Increasing the registry's storage capacity and adding mirror copies across regions
questions.explanation: Verifying signatures and provenance before deploy rejects unsigned or tampered artifacts. Storage, log retention and renaming do not authenticate the artifact.

questions.question: A legacy partner sends large XML messages to a cloud service, and a malformed message with an external entity reference crashed a parser last month. Which component would BEST filter such traffic before it reaches the application?
options: A hardware security module
A database activity monitor
An XML firewall that validates schemas and blocks malformed messages
A content delivery cache
questions.explanation: XML firewalls inspect and validate XML and SOAP traffic. HSMs protect keys, activity monitors watch database queries and caches speed delivery.

questions.question: A company exposes many internal services as APIs and wants one place to authenticate callers, rate limit and log requests, while each service still checks authorization for its own objects. Which component fits?
options: A honeypot
An API gateway in front of the services
A file integrity monitor
A bastion host
questions.explanation: A gateway centralizes authentication, throttling and logging at the edge. File integrity monitors, bastions and honeypots do not serve API traffic.

questions.question: A team needs to open email attachments from unknown senders to check for malware in the cloud, without any risk to production systems. What is the BEST approach?
options: Detonate them in an isolated sandbox with no route to production
Disable antivirus on a shared server so that the files cannot be quarantined during the test
Copy them to the production file share first
Open them on a developer's laptop, which has VPN access and a current antivirus tool
questions.explanation: Sandboxes isolate untrusted content with restricted permissions and network access. The other choices expose real systems.

questions.question: A SaaS application trusts sign-in assertions from an external identity provider. The provider's signing key is stolen. What is the MOST significant consequence?
options: Application logs begin to delete themselves automatically, hiding the signs of earlier logins
Only the provider's public marketing site is affected, because assertions never reach other applications
Users must pick much longer passwords for every federated application to stay safe
An attacker can forge assertions and sign in as any user across the federated applications
questions.explanation: Federation trusts the signed assertion, so a stolen signing key lets an attacker impersonate anyone in every relying application. The other outcomes are unrelated.

questions.question: A development team in a regulated company wants to avoid a single failure where both the code review and the build approval are done by the same person. Which principle does this support?
options: Weak coupling of services
Role stacking for efficiency
Separation of duties in the delivery pipeline
Security through obscurity
questions.explanation: Separating review from approval prevents one person from pushing unreviewed changes. Obscurity, loose coupling and stacking roles do not provide that control.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about functional and non-functional testing are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: Functional testing is the only type that can run in a pipeline
Security, performance and availability testing are non-functional
Security testing is outside the testing lifecycle
A feature can pass every functional test and still be exploitable
Non-functional testing checks only that features match the requirement document
questions.explanation: Functional testing checks behavior against requirements; security and other qualities are non-functional and both can be automated in pipelines.

questions.question: Which TWO measures help secure a continuous integration and delivery pipeline? (Choose two.)
options: A single long-lived administrator key shared by all jobs
Allowing build agents to reach any internal network without restriction
Protected branches with required reviews and signed artifacts
Storing secrets in the repository for easy access
Short-lived credentials with least privilege for build jobs
questions.explanation: Least-privilege short-lived credentials and protected, signed delivery limit what a compromise can do. Shared administrator keys, unrestricted agents and committed secrets are classic pipeline failures.

questions.question: Which THREE belong in third-party software management? (Choose three.)
options: Trusting any package with many downloads without verification
An inventory of every external component and service
Letting each developer decide silently which components to use
Tracking of vulnerabilities with a plan for replacement or patches
Vendor and license review before adoption
questions.explanation: Inventory, vendor and license review and vulnerability tracking are the foundation. Popularity is not verification and ad hoc decisions create blind spots.

questions.question: In the OWASP Top 10:2025, broken access control is still listed first.
questions.explanation: The 2025 edition keeps broken access control at number one and adds categories for supply chain failures and mishandling of exceptional conditions.

questions.question: The ASVS is a certification that an application passes once and keeps permanently.
questions.explanation: ASVS is a requirements and verification standard with levels; it is applied per application and revisited as the application changes.

questions.question: A white-box test requires access to the source code or design of the application.
questions.explanation: White-box testers have internal knowledge; black-box testers have none and gray-box testers have partial knowledge.

questions.question: An API gateway removes the need for each service to perform its own authorization checks.
questions.explanation: The gateway enforces edge policy, but object-level authorization must still be checked by the service.

questions.question: Signed build provenance helps detect that an artifact was not produced by the expected pipeline.
questions.explanation: Signature and provenance verification address integrity and authenticity in the supply chain.

questions.question: Compromise of a federated identity provider's signing key affects only one application.
questions.explanation: Every relying application that trusts the provider's signature is exposed.

questions.question: A new virtual machine image template exposes remote desktop and secure shell ports to the internet, has a default administrator password and logging disabled. Which principle was MOST clearly ignored?
options: Elastic scaling of resources
Secure by default configuration
Broad network access for customers
Resource pooling among tenants
questions.explanation: Safe initial settings (closed ports, no default credentials, logging on) define secure by default. Elasticity, pooling and broad access are cloud characteristics, not configuration principles.

questions.question: Administrators in a cloud environment need to manage servers in private subnets. Which design BEST limits exposure?
options: Public addresses on every server, protected only by strong passwords that are changed each quarter
Open inbound access from the whole internet to the management port
A single shared administrator account protected by a very long password stored in a team vault
A hardened bastion with multi-factor authentication and recorded sessions as the only entry point
questions.explanation: A controlled jump point reduces exposed surface and adds accountability. Public addresses, shared accounts and open ports increase attack surface.

questions.question: A hypervisor cluster must apply a firmware patch to one host without causing downtime for hosted applications. Which operational feature makes this possible?
options: Powering off the host immediately and restarting the guests once the update has finished
Deleting the guest virtual machines and rebuilding them from templates after the update
Disabling monitoring on the cluster so that the update does not trigger alerts and tickets
Placing the host in maintenance mode so workloads migrate to other hosts first
questions.explanation: Maintenance mode evacuates workloads before servicing, relying on cluster capacity. Powering off, disabling monitoring and deleting guests cause avoidable outage or blindness.

questions.question: A cluster's high availability configuration restarts virtual machines on surviving hosts after a node failure, but during a test several machines failed to restart. What is the MOST likely design flaw?
options: Insufficient reserved failover capacity on the remaining hosts
The virtual machines were too small to run their applications once the host recovered
The network used a VLAN
The hosts used encrypted storage, which prevents guests from being restarted on another host
questions.explanation: High availability needs spare capacity to absorb failed hosts' workloads. Encryption, small guests or VLANs do not prevent restarts.

questions.question: A monitoring dashboard shows one host's fan speed dropping and temperature rising. What is the BEST response?
options: Turn off hardware alerts for the whole fleet to reduce noise and operator fatigue
Raise the host's utilization to burn off the heat in the processor and the fans
Wait until the host crashes to confirm the problem and then rebuild it from a template
Migrate workloads away and repair the hardware before it fails
questions.explanation: Hardware monitoring exists to act before failure. Waiting, silencing alerts and increasing load make failure more likely.

questions.question: A team sees a sudden, sustained rise in compute usage in an account at night with no deployment scheduled. Which interpretation deserves FIRST attention?
options: A sign that the provider's service level has improved and fewer instances are needed
Possible abuse such as cryptomining through stolen credentials
Normal behavior of a scheduled change nobody recorded
A routine seasonal backup of the monitoring software
questions.explanation: Unexplained sustained usage is a classic abuse indicator and should be investigated. The other explanations ignore the absence of a recorded change.

questions.question: A security lead wants operating systems to stay in a known good state: documented settings, automated detection of deviations and prompt correction. Which cycle describes this?
options: Allow administrators to change settings freely whenever an application owner requests it
Patch only after an incident has shown that a weakness is exploited
Baseline, monitor and remediate against an approved configuration
Deploy once and archive the image, since a deployed system should never change
questions.explanation: Hardening is maintained by baselining, monitoring drift and remediating. One-time deployment, reactive patching and free changes allow drift.

questions.question: An organization wants a certifiable standard it can use to demonstrate a formal IT service management system, covering incident, change and service level processes. Which should it choose?
options: COBIT 2019
ISO/IEC 20000-1
CIS Critical Security Controls
ISO/IEC 27001
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 20000-1 specifies a service management system. ISO/IEC 27001 certifies an information security management system, COBIT is a governance framework and CIS Controls are prioritized safeguards.

questions.question: A board wants one framework to organize cybersecurity outcomes around govern, identify, protect, detect, respond and recover. Which is it?
options: The COSO internal control framework
ITIL 4
PCI DSS
NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
questions.explanation: CSF 2.0 organizes outcomes into those six functions, including the new Govern function. ITIL, PCI DSS and COSO have different structures and purposes.

questions.question: A small company with limited staff wants a prioritized set of safeguards that scales to its size, starting with essential hygiene. Which resource fits BEST?
options: A COBIT governance design built for a multinational with a large internal audit team
CIS Critical Security Controls using implementation groups
The full catalog of the NIST SP 800-53 high baseline applied to every system
A PCI DSS assessment covering all company data, not only payment card data
questions.explanation: CIS Controls implementation groups let smaller organizations start with essential safeguards. A high baseline catalog, an enterprise governance design and a payment assessment are not sized or targeted for that goal.

questions.question: A cloud provider needs to tell customers about a maintenance window and a security incident affecting several tenants. Which preparation BEST ensures consistent and timely communication?
options: Posting only on social media after the incident has already been reported in the press
Sending nothing to anyone until a regulator or a customer requests an explanation
Letting each engineer email affected customers individually with whatever details he or she has
Predefined stakeholder lists, channels and approved templates with named owners
questions.explanation: Planned channels, owners and approved wording make communication timely and consistent. Ad hoc emails, delayed posts and silence create legal and trust failures.

questions.question: Service restoration for a failing application succeeded within ten minutes, but the same failure recurred three times that week. Which ITIL-style process should now take over?
options: Capacity management, which plans resources and removes unused storage after the incident
Continuity management, which would relocate the data center to a different region
Release management, which ships more features in each release cycle
Problem management to find and remove the root cause
questions.explanation: Problem management addresses underlying causes of recurring incidents. Release, capacity and continuity management are separate processes.

questions.question: An investigator must collect evidence from a compromised workload and a cloud storage service whose provider logs sit outside the customer's control. Which preparation would have helped MOST?
options: A policy that evidence is gathered only after the incident is closed and approved by management
Pre-agreed forensic procedures and log access arrangements in the contract
A verbal promise from the provider's staff to retain all logs informally for as long as needed
Disabling logging in the affected accounts to avoid creating evidence that could be requested
questions.explanation: Forensic readiness depends on agreed procedures and access to provider-side data. Late collection, informal promises and disabled logging weaken or destroy evidence.

questions.question: A configuration management database lists server owners, but a post-incident review finds it was months out of date, slowing impact analysis. What is the BEST improvement?
options: Restricting updates to a single review at the end of each year to save effort
Removing owner and status fields from every entry to simplify the records
Printing the database every month and filing the report with the auditors
Automated discovery that continuously updates configuration items
questions.explanation: Cloud assets change constantly, so discovery must feed the record. Printing, annual updates and removing fields do not keep it accurate.

questions.question: Which TWO controls MOST directly harden remote administrative access to cloud virtual machines? (Choose two.)
options: Key- or certificate-based secure shell authentication with multi-factor authentication
Allowing remote desktop from any internet address
Leaving default accounts enabled
Routing access through a bastion host with session recording
Sharing one local administrator password among all engineers
questions.explanation: Strong authentication and a controlled, recorded entry point reduce risk. Open remote desktop, shared passwords and default accounts raise it.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about DNSSEC and VPNs are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: A VPN removes the need for authentication on the target systems
DNSSEC signs DNS records so resolvers can verify authenticity and integrity
Both provide protection for data at rest
A VPN encrypts traffic across an untrusted network but extends the network to the endpoint
DNSSEC encrypts the content of DNS queries for privacy
questions.explanation: DNSSEC gives authenticity and integrity, not confidentiality; VPNs protect data in transit but still require endpoint and identity controls. Neither protects data at rest.

questions.question: Which THREE belong in operating system hardening for cloud virtual machines? (Choose three.)
options: Leaving vendor default passwords for convenience
Monitoring for configuration drift
Running every service as an administrator
Applying an approved baseline such as a consensus benchmark
Removing unused services, accounts and ports
questions.explanation: Baselines, drift monitoring and attack surface reduction are core hardening steps. Default passwords and excessive privilege weaken systems.

questions.question: Which TWO activities are part of evidence management? (Choose two.)
options: Sharing evidence through a public link for convenience
Editing files on the original evidence drive to annotate them
Storing items in secured, access-controlled locations with integrity hashes
Assigning unique identifiers and logging every transfer of the item
questions.explanation: Tracking and secure storage preserve admissibility. Altering originals or sharing publicly destroys integrity.

questions.question: A honeypot is a preventive control that blocks attacks before they reach production.
questions.explanation: Honeypots detect and study attackers using decoys; they do not block traffic and must be isolated.

questions.question: Placing a host in maintenance mode lets its workloads migrate before servicing.
questions.explanation: This enables patching without downtime when the cluster has spare capacity.

questions.question: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 contains 93 controls grouped into four themes.
questions.explanation: The themes are organizational, people, physical and technological.

questions.question: DNSSEC provides confidentiality for DNS queries.
questions.explanation: DNSSEC provides authenticity and integrity of DNS data; query privacy needs encrypted DNS transport.

questions.question: Incident management and problem management are the same process with different names.
questions.explanation: Incident management restores service; problem management removes underlying causes of recurring incidents.

questions.question: COBIT 2019 is a governance and management framework for enterprise IT.
questions.explanation: COBIT 2019 from ISACA helps align IT with business goals and manage risk.

questions.question: Cluster resilience such as storage replication removes the need for backups.
questions.explanation: Replication copies deletions and corruption too; backups protect against them.

questions.question: A multinational stores European customer data in a European region of a US provider. A foreign authority orders the provider to hand over the data, while European law forbids that disclosure without a lawful basis. Which action BEST reduces the customer's exposure to this conflict?
options: Hold encryption keys under customer control and involve legal counsel to contest or narrow the demand
Move the data to whichever region is cheapest this quarter and review jurisdiction later
Disable all logging so that no records exist about the request or its handling
Agree to every request from any authority immediately to avoid penalties and delay
questions.explanation: Customer-held keys limit what the provider can produce and counsel manages the conflict through legal channels. Disabling logs hides evidence, price-driven region moves ignore law and automatic compliance may breach local law.
questions.whyTested: Conflicting legislation is a named topic and the answer is minimizing exposure plus legal escalation.

questions.question: A company needs a defensible method for forensic work after a cloud breach and wants standards covering collection of evidence, the suitability of the investigation method, analysis and the overall process. Which set of standards matches?
questions.explanation: The 27037 to 27043 series covers evidence handling, method assurance, analysis and investigation processes. The other sets cover management systems, continuity and risk, or product evaluation and cloud vocabulary and supplier relationships.

questions.question: A learning platform stores student grades and records for a US school district in a cloud service. Which law is MOST directly relevant to this data?
options: NERC CIP
PCI DSS
FERPA
HIPAA
questions.explanation: FERPA protects student education records. HIPAA covers health information, PCI DSS covers payment cards and NERC CIP covers the bulk electric system.

questions.question: A Canadian retailer uses a cloud analytics provider in another country to process customer purchase histories. Which statement about its accountability is MOST accurate under PIPEDA?
options: Accountability ends once the contract with the processor has been signed and filed
No accountability exists for private-sector data, because privacy law applies only to governments
The retailer remains accountable for personal information it transfers for processing, including abroad
Only the provider is accountable because it holds the data
questions.explanation: PIPEDA keeps the organization accountable for information in the hands of processors and requires comparable protection. The other statements deny continuing accountability.

questions.question: A company discovers a breach of electronic health records held by a business associate that stores them in the cloud. In which time frame must affected individuals generally be notified under US health privacy rules?
options: Within 72 hours to the individuals directly, regardless of the facts of the breach
Within 24 hours of the first alert, whether or not a breach is confirmed
Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery
Only after the next annual audit
questions.explanation: The breach notification rule requires notice without unreasonable delay and not later than 60 days after discovery. The 72-hour figure is the GDPR deadline for notifying the authority, not the individuals.

questions.question: A team begins planning a new service that profiles customers' behavior across devices. Which activity BEST identifies privacy risks to individuals and the controls to address them before launch?
options: A privacy impact assessment performed during design
A cost estimate performed by procurement during vendor selection
A penetration test performed shortly after launch by an external team
A disaster recovery drill performed after launch to rehearse the failover plan
questions.explanation: A privacy impact assessment at design time finds risks to individuals and changes the design. The other activities test security, recovery or cost.

questions.question: An auditor reviewing a SaaS provider's SOC report notes that it covers only the provider's main application and excludes the analytics module the customer actually uses. What should the customer do?
options: Assume the whole provider is covered by the clean opinion, since the auditor signed it
Treat the analytics module as unassured, ask for scope extension or compensating evidence and apply customer controls
Ignore the exclusion, because audit reports do not list scope and apply to every service
Accept the report as it stands, because it was issued by a well-known audit firm
questions.explanation: Scope statements define what is assured; excluded services need other evidence. A clean opinion on one service does not extend to another, and the firm's reputation does not change scope.

questions.question: A company wants a report on a provider's controls that is relevant to financial reporting and is available under an international standard rather than a US one. Which pairing is MOST accurate?
options: ISAE 3000 produces a SOC 1 report only
ISAE 3402 corresponds to SOC 1 under SSAE 18
SSAE 18 corresponds to ISO/IEC 27018 certification
ISAE 3402 corresponds to a PCI assessment
questions.explanation: ISAE 3402 is the international standard for reports on controls relevant to financial reporting, equivalent in role to SOC 1 under SSAE 18. The other pairings mismatch standards.

questions.question: A company's security leader wants control owners to evaluate their own risks and controls regularly, with independent validation afterwards, to keep ownership close to the business. Which technique is this?
options: Risk and control self-assessment
A disaster recovery full interruption test
A black-box penetration test
A business impact analysis
questions.explanation: Risk and control self-assessment lets control owners assess themselves and is then validated independently. Penetration testing, recovery tests and BIAs are different activities.

questions.question: A utility moves a monitoring system for part of the bulk electric system to a cloud service. Which regulatory regime MUST the project consider?
options: NERC CIP standards
FERPA
GAPP
SOX Section 404
questions.explanation: NERC CIP sets mandatory cybersecurity requirements for bulk electric system entities. FERPA concerns education records, SOX concerns financial reporting and GAPP is a privacy framework.

questions.question: A risk manager must decide how to treat the possibility of a long outage at a critical SaaS vendor. The company agrees to run part of the workload with a second vendor under a contract that divides the consequences. Which treatment is this?
options: Risk elimination
Risk sharing
Risk avoidance
Risk acceptance
questions.explanation: Sharing divides the consequence with another party. Avoidance stops the activity, acceptance bears it silently and elimination is not a standard treatment.

questions.question: A business rule says that a cloud provider's breach notice must reach the customer faster than the customer's own regulatory deadline. Which place BEST captures this requirement?
options: The customer's internal wiki, which describes the provider's duties as the customer understands them
The provider's public marketing page describing how quickly incidents are handled
The contract's breach notification clause with a shorter notice period than the regulatory deadline
An informal email from the account manager promising prompt notice of any incident
questions.explanation: Contract terms make notice periods enforceable. Marketing pages, informal emails and internal wikis do not bind the provider.

questions.question: A software company depends on a small vendor for a critical component and fears the vendor may fail financially. Which contractual protection BEST addresses this risk?
options: A warranty that the vendor will never go out of business, stated in the contract
A promise to review the vendor annually without access to its materials
A non-disclosure agreement alone, signed by the vendor and the customer's legal team
Escrow of source code or configuration with a neutral party, with release conditions
questions.explanation: Escrow gives access to critical assets if the vendor fails. Warranties of permanence, reviews without access and NDAs do not secure continuity.

questions.question: A company's cloud policy states which services may be bought, which data classes they may hold and who approves exceptions. What problem is this policy MOST directly designed to reduce?
options: License fees for operating systems
Hardware failure in the provider's data center
Latency between two cloud regions
Unsanctioned shadow IT adoption
questions.explanation: A cloud computing policy defines acceptable services, data classes and approvals, which limits shadow IT. The other problems are technical or financial.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about audit scope statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: A clean opinion covers all services the provider sells
A report assures only the services, locations and period named in its scope
Customer-side controls are often excluded and must be implemented by the customer
Excluded subservice organizations are automatically assured
Scope statements are written for marketing and can be ignored
questions.explanation: Scope limits what is assured, and users must supply their own complementary controls. Other statements overstate coverage.

questions.question: Which TWO items appear among the privacy frameworks and standards named for cloud privacy requirements? (Choose two.)
options: ISO/IEC 27036 as a privacy law
Generally Accepted Privacy Principles with ten principles
NERC CIP as a data subject rights regulation
Common Criteria as a privacy framework
ISO/IEC 27018 for protecting personal data in public clouds
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 27018 and GAPP are privacy standards or frameworks. ISO/IEC 27036 concerns supplier relationships, NERC CIP is electric sector security and Common Criteria evaluates products.

questions.question: Which THREE items belong in a cloud contract to support exit and accountability? (Choose three.)
options: Right to audit or access to independent assurance reports
Data return and deletion terms with evidence of deletion
A ban on the customer ever terminating the contract
Breach notification timelines and subprocessor controls
A clause stating the provider owns customer data
questions.explanation: Data return, notification, subprocessor and audit terms support exit and accountability. Provider data ownership and no termination undermine the customer.

questions.question: HIPAA breach notification to individuals may take place up to 60 days after discovery of a breach, but must not be unreasonably delayed.
questions.explanation: The rule requires notice without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 days.

questions.question: A privacy impact assessment is performed before a system launches so privacy risks to individuals can change the design.
questions.explanation: It is a design-time review; the DPIA is the GDPR's formal version for high-risk processing.

questions.question: A SOC report that excludes a subservice organization assures the controls of that subservice organization.
questions.explanation: Excluded subservice organizations are not assured by the report; customers need other evidence.

questions.question: A master service agreement sets general terms while a statement of work defines specific deliverables.
questions.explanation: The SOW operates under the MSA; the SLA sets measurable service levels.

questions.question: Risk transfer and risk sharing are interchangeable terms in the outline's list of treatments.
questions.explanation: The outline lists avoid, mitigate, transfer, share and accept as separate treatments.

questions.question: PCI DSS version 4.0.1 is the current version of the standard.
questions.explanation: Version 4.0.1 is the current edition of the PCI Data Security Standard.

questions.question: ISO/IEC 27050 is a standard for electronic discovery.
questions.explanation: It is a multi-part standard covering the eDiscovery process from identification to production.

questions.question: An attacker who gains rights in the orchestration layer of a cloud platform could create, change and delete large numbers of workloads in one operation. Which control BEST protects this building block?
options: Larger virtual machine sizes so the orchestrator has spare capacity during attacks
Additional storage replicas in a second region so that deleted workloads can be rebuilt
Column-level encryption of every database that the orchestrated workloads can reach
Strong authentication, least privilege, approvals and full logging on orchestration and management calls
questions.explanation: Orchestration acts with broad privilege, so access to it needs the tightest identity controls and auditing. Database encryption, replicas and capacity do not stop a malicious operation from being issued.
questions.whyTested: Maps outline objective 1.1 building block technologies to the control that fits each one.

questions.question: A provider lets customers upload their own code and runs it on a managed runtime while operating the servers and operating system. Under the ISO/IEC 17788 capability types, what does the customer receive?
options: Platform capabilities, because customers deploy and run their own code on the provider's runtime
Infrastructure capabilities, because customers provision and manage the virtual machines themselves
None of the three, because managed runtimes fall outside the capability model entirely
Application capabilities, because the provider supplies the finished software that customers merely use
questions.explanation: Deploying customer code on a provider-managed runtime is a platform capability. Infrastructure capabilities leave the operating system to the customer, and application capabilities mean using the provider's own software.
questions.whyTested: Tests classification of cloud service capabilities as the outline describes them.

questions.question: A product team wants a new managed service to be safe without customers having to tune it: minimal exposed functionality, restrictive settings and secure behavior out of the box. Which design approach describes this?
options: Shift-right testing that finds weaknesses only after customers report them
Secure by design and secure by default
Defense by compliance checklist completed shortly before general availability
Security through obscurity combined with a detailed configuration hardening guide
questions.explanation: Secure by design builds protection into the architecture and secure by default ships with safe settings, so the customer does not carry the burden. A hardening guide pushes the work to customers, and late testing or checklists add little.
questions.whyTested: Covers the outline's secure-by-design cloud design pattern.

questions.question: A DevOps team releases many times a day, yet security reviews happen only before quarterly milestones and have become a backlog. What is the BEST way to keep security in step with delivery?
options: Defer security work until after release and fix issues only when customers report them
Move all security staff into a separate gate team that approves every individual change by hand
Build automated security checks into the pipeline and share ownership of findings with developers
Cut the release frequency to the number of reviews the security team can handle each quarter
questions.explanation: DevSecOps brings checks to where changes happen, such as scanning and policy gates, so feedback is fast and scales. Throttling releases, manual gates and post-release fixing do not scale or are too late.
questions.whyTested: Tests the DevOps security bullet of objective 1.4.

questions.question: A security team's machine learning model flags unusual network behavior. After the company migrates many workloads to a new architecture, the model begins missing attacks. What is the MOST likely cause and response?
options: Model drift on the new traffic patterns, so validate against current data and retrain
A flaw in the cloud provider's hypervisor, so open a ticket with the provider and wait for a platform patch to be released
Normal behavior, since models never need review once they pass their first validation
Excess encryption of network flows, so disable TLS to restore full visibility to the model
questions.explanation: A model trained on old traffic degrades when behavior changes; monitoring performance and retraining on validated, representative data restores it. Disabling TLS and waiting for a patch address nothing, and models need ongoing review.
questions.whyTested: Covers AI-based cloud threat detection and the need to verify its data sources.

questions.question: A hiring tool built on a cloud machine learning service ranks candidates, and an audit finds consistently lower scores for one protected group. Which response BEST addresses the ethical concern?
options: Hide the demographic fields from the audit report so the ranking appears neutral to reviewers and the regulator
Rely on the cloud provider's SOC 2 report as evidence that the model outputs are fair
Examine the training data for bias, test fairness, document the results and add human oversight
Keep the model but encrypt the scoring results so that candidates cannot question them
questions.explanation: Bias usually comes from data and features, so the fix is analysis, fairness testing, documentation and human review. Hiding fields, citing an infrastructure report or encrypting results leaves the harm in place.
questions.whyTested: Tests the ethical concerns bullet of the AI and machine learning objective.

questions.question: A security orchestration playbook automatically disables any account that triggers a high-severity alert. Analysts fear false positives will lock out executives and critical service accounts. Which design is BEST?
options: Tier the response: automate low-impact actions, add approval for high-impact accounts
Exempt all privileged accounts from every alert so the playbook can never cause an outage
Remove automation entirely, since SOAR tools should only ever produce reports for analysts
Keep full automation and ask affected executives to open a ticket if they are locked out
questions.explanation: Risk-based tiers keep the speed of automation while limiting the blast radius of an incorrect action. Removing automation loses the benefit, exempting privileged accounts opens the biggest hole, and ignoring false positives harms the business.
questions.whyTested: Checks judgment about SOAR trade-offs between speed and safety.

questions.question: Using a managed AI service removes the customer's need to assess regulatory requirements that apply to how the AI output is used.
questions.explanation: The customer remains accountable for lawful use, such as high-risk classifications under the EU AI Act, whichever party runs the model.

questions.question: A provider stores archive objects as erasure-coded fragments spread across several regions so that any subset of fragments can rebuild the object. What is the MOST important consideration for a customer with residency rules?
options: Dispersion removes the need for encryption because no single site holds a complete and usable copy of the object
Dispersion guarantees that the object stays inside one country because fragments are small
Dispersion makes deletion instant because every fragment expires automatically at exactly the same moment everywhere
Dispersion aids availability and limits single-site exposure, but fragment locations may breach residency rules
questions.explanation: Splitting data improves resilience and reduces what any one location reveals, yet fragments in other regions can still conflict with residency requirements. It does not replace encryption or guarantee jurisdiction.
questions.whyTested: Tests data dispersion against data location and residency duties.

questions.question: An investigator reviewing storage access logs finds the action and timestamp for each event, but cannot tell who performed it or from where. Which attributes were missing from the event definition?
options: Encryption algorithm, key length and certificate expiry date of the object
Retention period, storage class and billing tag attached to the bucket
Disk block size, file system type and data center rack identifier
Identity of the actor, source IP address and geolocation
questions.explanation: Auditability needs who, from where and when. Storage mechanics, algorithms and billing metadata do not attribute an action to an actor or a place.
questions.whyTested: Covers event sources and required event attributes in objective 2.8.

questions.question: A company plans to fine-tune a model on support chats that contain personal data. Which control BEST reduces the risk that the finished model reveals individual records?
options: Encrypt the training volume at rest and leave the dataset content unchanged
Place the model endpoint in a private subnet and keep every record in the dataset
Minimize and de-identify the training data, then test the model for memorization
Increase the number of training epochs so that the model learns each record thoroughly and reliably
questions.explanation: Leakage comes from what the model memorizes, so reducing and de-identifying data and testing for extraction address it directly. Storage encryption and network placement protect the container, and more training increases memorization.
questions.whyTested: Tests dataset and model privacy under objective 2.9.

questions.question: Spreading erasure-coded fragments of data across regions can conflict with data residency requirements even though no single region holds the whole object.
questions.explanation: Residency rules concern where personal or regulated data is stored or processed, so fragment placement still has to be approved.

questions.question: A regional bank is choosing a site for a data center that must stay available through regional disasters. Which factor is MOST relevant to the decision?
options: Whether the building was previously used for light industry rather than for ordinary office space
Proximity of the site to the bank's executive offices for easier ceremonial visits
Natural hazard exposure, diversity of power and carriers, and the legal jurisdiction of the site
The availability of the cheapest rack space regardless of utility diversity
questions.explanation: Physical design is about hazard exposure, utilities, connectivity and jurisdiction, weighed with buy-or-build economics. Convenience and bargain space do not support resilience.
questions.whyTested: Tests the physical design bullet of the secure data center objective.

questions.question: A provider hosts competing retailers on shared hosts. Which logical design measure MOST directly keeps their traffic and data apart?
options: A single flat network where each retailer's workloads are told apart by naming conventions
Host firewalls configured identically on every host so that all tenants share the same rules and rule sets
One shared administrative account for all tenants, with tags to record who did what
Tenant-specific virtual networks, identities and keys with isolation enforced by policy
questions.explanation: Tenant partitioning relies on separate networks, identities and keys enforced by the platform. Naming, shared accounts and uniform firewalls provide labels rather than isolation.
questions.whyTested: Covers logical design and tenant partitioning.

questions.question: A site buys connectivity from two carriers, but both circuits enter the building through the same underground conduit. Which design weakness does this show?
options: Carrier diversity matters only for voice traffic and has no bearing on data availability
Dual carriers create a risk of data corruption because packets arrive out of order
Two carriers are unnecessary because a single provider with a premium contract is always safer
The pathways are not diverse, so one physical cut or fire could sever both carriers
questions.explanation: Multi-vendor pathway connectivity means carriers use physically separate routes; a shared conduit is a single point of failure. The other statements are incorrect claims about carriers.
questions.whyTested: Tests environmental and resilience design for connectivity.

questions.question: During risk assessment of a new cloud platform a team has listed its assets, the threats against them and the vulnerabilities present. What is the NEXT step in analysis?
options: Transfer all identified risks to an insurer before they have been rated
Accept every risk that has a low purchase price for the corresponding safeguard
Estimate the likelihood and impact of each scenario to rate and rank the risks
Select the provider's default controls and treat the assessment as complete
questions.explanation: Identification is followed by analysis of likelihood and impact, which supports ranking and treatment decisions. Accepting, transferring or defaulting before rating skips the reasoning that treatment depends on.
questions.whyTested: Covers risk assessment steps for cloud infrastructure.

questions.question: After a regional failover the standby region delivers only 40 percent of normal capacity for the first day. Which recovery planning concept does this describe?
options: Recovery point objective, the amount of data loss that is tolerable
Recovery time objective, the time allowed to restore the service
Recovery service level, the degree of service delivered after recovery
Mean time between failures, the average time before the next failure
questions.explanation: Recovery service level states how much functionality or capacity must be available once recovery completes. RPO is about data loss, RTO about time and MTBF about reliability.
questions.whyTested: Tests the recovery service level term in objective 3.5.

questions.question: Auditors need to reconstruct a network incident that crossed several cloud accounts. Which audit mechanism set is MOST useful?
options: Screenshots of the console taken by administrators when they remember to do so
Centralized, time-synchronized log collection with correlation and retained flow logs or captures
Only the provider's annual availability report, which lists uptime by region
Separate local logs on each workload that are overwritten after a few hours
questions.explanation: Central, time-synchronized and correlated logs plus network records allow reconstruction across accounts. Local rotating logs, ad hoc screenshots and an uptime report cannot show who did what.
questions.whyTested: Covers audit mechanisms such as log collection, correlation and packet capture.

questions.question: A cloud customer using IaaS remains responsible for physical access controls at the provider's data center.
questions.explanation: Physical and environmental protection of the facility is the provider's duty; the customer verifies it through audit reports and contracts.

questions.question: A team moving from waterfall to agile worries that end-of-project security reviews will block each sprint. What is the BEST approach?
options: Put security requirements, threat modeling and automated tests in every iteration and in the definition of done
Skip threat modeling entirely because agile teams prefer working software over analysis
Ask the security team to approve every user story before the sprint can start
Keep a single security review after the final sprint and treat all earlier work as draft
questions.explanation: Agile needs security tasks inside each iteration and acceptance criteria, rather than a late gate. A single late review finds problems too late, and per-story approvals do not scale.
questions.whyTested: Contrasts waterfall and agile security activities in the secure SDLC objective.

questions.question: An authenticated API user changes the invoice number in a request and receives another customer's invoice. Which OWASP API Security Top 10 risk is this?
options: Broken object level authorization
Unrestricted resource consumption of the invoice service
Improper inventory management of retired API versions
Security misconfiguration of the web server headers
questions.explanation: The API checks who the caller is but not whether they may access that specific object, which is broken object level authorization, the top API risk. The other risks involve load, configuration or old versions.
questions.whyTested: Applies the API Security Top 10 named in objective 4.1.

questions.question: The CWE Top 25 ranks the most dangerous software weakness types using vulnerability data, and it complements the OWASP Top 10 rather than replacing it.
questions.explanation: It lists weakness classes by prevalence and severity, while the OWASP list is an awareness document of web application risk categories.

questions.question: A customer's regulated workload runs on shared cloud hardware, and the compliance officer worries about the provider's own administrators. Which treatment fits the cloud-specific risk BEST?
options: Store the encryption keys in the same account as the data for convenience of recovery
Move the workload to a larger instance type that is harder for administrators to see
Use customer-held keys, restrict and log provider access and review the provider's insider controls
Accept the risk because provider staff are certified and therefore cannot access any customer data
questions.explanation: Customer-held keys, logged access and assurance about provider controls reduce provider insider exposure. Certification does not prevent access, instance size does not hide data and co-locating keys with data weakens separation.
questions.whyTested: Tests cloud-specific risks such as CSP insider threats and lack of visibility.

questions.question: A QA team's functional tests all pass, yet a user can bypass a payment step by replaying an earlier request. Which testing gap does this reveal?
options: Compatibility testing was missing, because older browsers do not enforce payment steps
Usability testing was missing, because replay depends on a confusing interface
Load testing was missing, because replay attacks only occur under heavy traffic
Abuse case testing was missing, because functional tests only confirm intended behavior
questions.explanation: Abuse and misuse cases deliberately try to break rules the way an attacker would, while functional tests confirm that expected paths work. The other test types do not look for deliberate bypass.
questions.whyTested: Covers abuse case testing and QA in objective 4.4.

questions.question: During QA test runs a team wants security findings tied to the exact line of code that handled the request, found by instrumenting the running application. Which technique fits?
options: Interactive application security testing
Static application security testing alone, because it executes the application in production
Software composition analysis, because it reports where tainted data flows at runtime
A tabletop exercise, because it traces requests through the compiled application
questions.explanation: IAST instruments a running application and reports vulnerabilities with code context. SAST analyzes code without running it, SCA inventories components and a tabletop is a discussion.
questions.whyTested: Distinguishes IAST from SAST, DAST and SCA.

questions.question: A customer wants a repeatable weekly inventory of known weaknesses across hundreds of virtual machines, ranked by severity. Which activity is the BEST fit?
options: An annual penetration test limited to the internet-facing web application of the business
A tabletop exercise on the ransomware response plan
A red team exercise that attempts to reach executives' mailboxes
An authenticated vulnerability scan with results tracked to remediation
questions.explanation: Assessments are broad, repeatable and rank known weaknesses; penetration tests and red team exercises are narrower and prove exploitability, and tabletops rehearse response.
questions.whyTested: Separates vulnerability assessment from penetration testing in objective 5.6.

questions.question: Before running a penetration test against workloads in a public cloud, the customer should confirm the provider's testing policy and obtain written authorization.
questions.explanation: Unauthorized testing can breach contract and law, and scope must avoid attacking the provider's shared infrastructure.

questions.question: A SOC receives thousands of alerts with no context and cannot tell which matter. Which improvement would MOST help prioritization?
options: Extending log retention from ninety days to seven years without changing alert content
Feeding curated threat intelligence into the SIEM and SOAR tools to enrich alerts with context
Turning off all low-severity detections so that analysts only see the most severe signals
Replacing analyst review with a single static firewall rule set for all environments
questions.explanation: Threat intelligence adds context such as known indicators and adversary behavior, which helps rank alerts. Longer retention, disabled detections and static rules do not give context.
questions.whyTested: Covers threat intelligence within log capture and analysis.

questions.question: A machine-learning anomaly detector reports nothing for weeks, until it emerges that an administrator quietly disabled rules on a network security group and turned off flow logging. What was overlooked?
options: Monitoring must also verify that controls and log sources are active and alert on changes
Anomaly detectors should be replaced by manual review of every packet that crosses the network boundary
Administrators should hold no privileges at all, which removes the need for monitoring
The detector should be trained on fewer features so that it generates fewer alerts
questions.explanation: Intelligent monitoring includes watching the health of the controls and telemetry that feed it, so a silent change is itself an alert. Packet-level manual review and zero privileges are impractical, and fewer features do not fix blind spots.
questions.whyTested: Tests intelligent monitoring of security controls.

questions.question: All hosts in a cluster are healthy, but a guest virtual machine has stopped responding because of an operating system fault. Which measure addresses guest OS availability?
options: Guest health monitoring with automatic restart and tested guest backups
Placing the host in maintenance mode so that the guest migrates to a different server in the cluster
Adding more physical storage to the cluster to increase raw capacity
Raising the hypervisor patch level on every host in the cluster
questions.explanation: Host clustering protects against host failure, so a faulty guest needs its own health checks, restart logic and recoverable backups. Maintenance mode, extra storage and host patching do not fix a guest fault.
questions.whyTested: Covers availability of the guest operating system.

questions.question: A cluster automatically moves virtual machines between hosts to balance load and keep response times steady. Which capability is this?
options: Snapshot scheduling to preserve guest state at fixed times
Maintenance mode used to evacuate a host before servicing
Distributed resource scheduling or dynamic optimization
Storage replication to a secondary site for disaster recovery
questions.explanation: Distributed resource scheduling places and rebalances workloads automatically. Maintenance mode is for planned servicing, replication provides recovery and snapshots preserve state.
questions.whyTested: Tests clustered host availability features.

questions.question: After a major outage an organization wants a standing practice that turns incident reviews and audit findings into tracked, measured improvements. Which ITIL practice is this?
options: Continual service improvement
Release management
Capacity management
Deployment management
questions.explanation: Continual improvement measures service results and converts lessons into owned actions. Release and deployment management control how changes go live, and capacity management plans resource demand.
questions.whyTested: Covers the continual service improvement management item of objective 5.6.

questions.question: A firm wants a general enterprise risk management standard of principles, framework and process that is not specific to IT. Which should it choose?
options: ISO/IEC 27001, which certifies an information security management system
A SOC 2 report, which attests to a service provider's controls
PCI DSS, which sets requirements for protecting payment card data
questions.explanation: ISO 31000 is the general risk management guideline. ISO/IEC 27001 is security-management specific, PCI DSS is a payment standard and a SOC 2 report is an attestation, not a framework to adopt.
questions.whyTested: Tests recognition of risk frameworks in objective 6.4.

questions.question: Which indicator would be the MOST useful key risk indicator for the risk of cloud misconfiguration?
options: The number of cloud provider marketing emails received by the security team
The trend in publicly exposed storage and critical findings open past their deadline
Annual revenue of the business units that use the cloud environment
The total number of employees who work in the cloud engineering department
questions.explanation: A key risk indicator signals rising exposure early and links to the risk, such as exposed resources and overdue findings. Headcount, revenue and marketing volume say nothing about misconfiguration.
questions.whyTested: Applies metrics for risk management.

questions.question: A company buys cyber risk insurance and concludes that its security controls can be reduced. Which statement is MOST accurate?
options: Insurance transfers part of the financial loss, insurers expect baseline controls and accountability stays
Insurance removes the likelihood of an incident, which makes risk assessment unnecessary
Insurance eliminates regulatory fines in every jurisdiction regardless of how the incident arose
Insurance shifts legal accountability to the cloud provider, so customer controls become optional
questions.explanation: Insurance is risk transfer of some financial impact, often conditional on controls and subject to exclusions. It does not remove accountability, likelihood or the need to assess risk.
questions.whyTested: Tests risk transfer through contract and insurance.

questions.question: A provider is compelled by a foreign court order to hand over customer data stored in another country, which conflicts with the customer's home-country law. Which treatment BEST reduces this legal risk?
options: Rely on the provider's public statement that it never discloses customer data to any government
Remove the data location clause so that the contract is shorter and simpler
Hold encryption keys under customer control and require notice and challenge rights
Store the data in a region chosen only for the lowest price per gigabyte
questions.explanation: Customer-held keys limit what the provider can disclose and contract terms for notice and challenge give a response path. Marketing claims, price-driven location and a missing clause increase exposure.
questions.whyTested: Covers conflicting legislation and legal risks specific to cloud.

questions.question: When two countries' laws conflict over the handling of data, a contract clause alone resolves the conflict because courts always honor the agreed terms.
questions.explanation: Mandatory law and regulators can override contract terms, so conflicts need legal analysis, location choices and technical controls.

questions.question: An auditor must plan an engagement for a SaaS provider with no on-site access. What should the plan define FIRST?
options: Scope, objectives and evidence sources such as provider reports, logs and API evidence
The final audit opinion, so that fieldwork can be limited to supporting it
Whether to skip the plan and perform only a walkthrough of the provider's website
A list of physical data centers to visit regardless of what the provider allows
questions.explanation: Planning for a cloud audit depends on agreeing scope and objectives and identifying evidence that can actually be obtained remotely. Fixing the opinion first or insisting on site visits is neither possible nor independent.
questions.whyTested: Tests audit planning adapted for the cloud.

questions.question: A customer compares a provider's SOC 2 report with its own policy and finds five requirements unmet. What is the BEST next activity?
options: Terminate the contract at once, since any gap makes the provider unusable
Ask the provider to rewrite the report so that it matches the customer's policy
Document the gaps and choose a treatment for each, such as compensating controls or contract changes
Ignore the gaps, because a SOC 2 report is a certification that the provider can never fail or lose
questions.explanation: A gap analysis ends in documented treatment decisions. Reports cannot be rewritten, ignoring gaps is unsafe and automatic termination is disproportionate.
questions.whyTested: Applies gap analysis and control self-assessment.

questions.question: Which role is responsible for the day-to-day quality, definitions and metadata of a dataset, working under the data owner's policy?
options: Regulator
Data subject
Data steward
Data processor
questions.explanation: A data steward maintains quality and definitions for the owner. A processor handles data for a controller, the subject is the individual the data describes and a regulator supervises compliance.
questions.whyTested: Tests the difference between data roles such as owner, controller, custodian, processor and steward.

questions.question: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 refers to organizations that decide the purpose of processing as data fiduciaries and to individuals as data principals.
questions.explanation: These are the Act's equivalents of controller and data subject, with a Data Protection Board enforcing the law.

lessons.title: Cloud Foundations and Shared Responsibility
lessons.summary: What makes something cloud, the service and deployment models, who is responsible for what, and the emerging technologies (AI, confidential computing) the newer outline folds in.
lessons.reading:
Cloud computing is a way of renting computing power instead of owning it. The formal definition used by the exam, from NIST, names five essential characteristics: on-demand self-service (you provision resources yourself, without filing a ticket), broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity and measured service. If a vendor hosts a server for you but you must phone them to resize it and pay a flat monthly fee, that is hosting, not cloud. The characteristic that most shapes security is resource pooling, because it produces multi-tenancy: many customers sharing the same physical machines, separated only by software. Isolation between tenants is therefore a cornerstone of cloud security and a favorite exam topic.

Cloud services come in three service models that differ in how much of the technology stack the provider runs for you. In infrastructure as a service you get virtual machines, storage and networks and manage everything from the guest operating system upward. In platform as a service the provider also runs the operating system and runtime, and you bring only your application and data. In software as a service you simply use a finished application. As you move from infrastructure to software, the provider takes over more of the stack and you give up control. That trade is the heart of the shared responsibility model: the provider secures the cloud itself (facilities, hardware, hypervisor, core services) and the customer secures what they put in the cloud and how they configure it. The line moves with the service model, but a few things never move. Data, identities and access decisions, and the choice of settings are always the customer's, and accountability to regulators cannot be handed to anyone.

Deployment models describe who owns and shares the environment. A public cloud is open to many customers. A private cloud serves one organization. A hybrid cloud binds two different models together so workloads and data can move between them, and a community cloud is shared by organizations with a common concern, such as the same regulator. Multi-cloud is a different idea altogether: using more than one provider.

Architects also weigh vendor lock-in. Portability, interoperability and reversibility are the properties that keep an exit possible, and the ISO/IEC 17789 cross-cutting aspects (auditability, availability, governance, privacy, regulatory, resiliency, security, service levels and more) act as a checklist of things to consider before adopting any service.

The outline also asks how newer technologies change the picture. Artificial intelligence and machine learning make training data, models and prompts into assets to classify and protect, and the customer keeps responsibility for them even on a fully managed service. Confidential computing protects data in use by running code inside a hardware-based trusted execution environment. Quantum computing threatens today's public-key algorithms, which is why architects favor crypto agility. Underlying all of this are three design principles to reach for in almost any scenario: defense in depth, least privilege and zero trust, in which identity rather than network location decides who gets in.

The outline treats the reference architecture as a map of roles and activities. The customer, the provider, the partner (such as an auditor, a service developer or a broker) and the regulator each perform different activities, so a control only works when someone owns it. ISO/IEC 17788 also describes what a customer receives as capability types: infrastructure capabilities (compute, storage and network), platform capabilities (a managed runtime for your code) and application capabilities (finished software). Underneath, every service is assembled from building blocks such as virtualization, storage, networking, databases and orchestration, and each block carries its own isolation and configuration risks.

Secure design draws on classic principles (least privilege, defense in depth, fail-safe defaults, separation of duties, complete mediation) that SANS and similar guidance teach, on provider Well-Architected frameworks, on the CSA Enterprise Architecture and on the idea of secure by design and secure by default. DevOps security means building automated checks and shared ownership into the pipeline rather than reviewing at the end. Business impact analysis, with cost-benefit analysis and return on investment, justifies the spend on continuity and recovery, and the CSA Top Threats report is a useful list of what goes wrong most often: misconfiguration and change control, identity and access, and insecure interfaces lead the 2024 edition.
